content: Purchasing in healthcare involves the systems and mechanisms used to allocate pooled funds for the provision of health services. These funds are utilized by providers to deliver specific benefits to the population. Purchasing is a fundamental function of any health system, and transitioning from passive to strategic purchasing is a key focus of health financing reforms in many countries, as it is essential for sustainability. In light of declining donor funding, countries must take a leading role in mobilizing, allocating, and managing resources. Cost should not be a barrier, especially for adolescents, who face multiple barriers to care. Key actions for financing include promoting VMMC as part of national essential service packages, estimating country-specific resource needs, integrating VMMC into national health operational plans, increasing domestic resources, harmonizing donor-funded elements with national budgets, and ensuring transparency and accountability in health financing systems. Additionally, partnerships with the private sector and regional resource mobilization options should be explored to support sustainability. In terms of service purchasing, healthcare providers should be remunerated using approaches that encourage effectiveness and quality, with adjustments for risk and income. VMMC services should be included in health insurance schemes, and strategies should be developed to integrate these services into both public and private insurance systems. The private sector should be considered a partner, and new financing sources from this sector should be explored. This requires integrating VMMC into national health workforce planning, addressing issues such as skill mix, distribution, retention, workload, and rural coverage, and considering gender, ethics, and worker safety in the selection, training, and deployment of health workers. Pre-service and continuing education should include VMMC content, particularly for nurses and other relevant cadres, and training curricula should align with regulated scopes of practice. Management, support, and supervision of the health workforce are essential to maintaining an efficient and effective system. This includes strong personnel management, recruitment, performance monitoring, and supportive supervision focused on adolescent-friendly, integrated services. Countries must address challenges in identifying and training sufficient personnel and engage community health workers and volunteers to sustain demand for VMMC services. Strategic information systems are critical for the sustainability of VMMC programs. Countries need to transition from donor-dependent, parallel systems to integrated, country-owned systems for data collection and use. Efficient data collection methods, such as electronic systems, should replace paper-based systems, and data management should promote country-level ownership. Safety monitoring systems are vital for detecting, reporting, and responding to adverse events (AEs) related to circumcision procedures. These systems should include clear definitions of AEs and mechanisms for evaluation and response. Clinical staff should be closely engaged in safety monitoring efforts. Sustainable supplies and equipment are essential for VMMC service delivery. Procurement and distribution systems should be integrated into national supply chains, and quality assurance mechanisms should maintain the safety and efficacy of supplies. Proper waste management systems must also be established to handle healthcare waste effectively. Leadership and governance are critical for sustaining VMMC services. Ministries of Health (MOH) should take a leading role in program ownership, coordination, and accountability. This includes engaging subnational and local leaders, establishing partnerships for advocacy and implementation, and integrating VMMC into national health strategies and operational plans. Intersectoral coordination with sectors such as education, civil society, and the private sector is essential to achieving shared objectives. Finally, service delivery must prioritize accessibility, acceptability, equity, and effectiveness. Adolescent-friendly VMMC services should meet the diverse needs and preferences of adolescents.
